STONE ATELIER / DESIGN STUDY

Natural materials.
Individual character.

Five pieces, imagined in five complete interiors. Explore a room, move closer to the furniture, and compare stone and metal finishes in real time.

Two ways to explore

Photographic shows a Blender-rendered daylight room with your selected stone and metal. Live render is designed for desktop and laptop use. Daylight combines prepared Blender lighting with camera-dependent tabletop reflections, so movement stays clear without waiting for grain to settle. Stone, metal, and oak choices remain interactive. The Grand Salon adds a round dining table with three base designs, two furniture collections, rug palettes and chair upholstery. These additional choices are available in Live render. Evening uses progressive, noise-filtered lighting and may need time to refine. The rooms are design studies, not a claim of photographic equivalence. The piece zooms into the photograph; switch to Live render to see other angles.

How to explore

Drag to orbit. Scroll or pinch to zoom. Use Room view for the setting, The piece for a closer look, or Fit room to reset the framing. On a keyboard, focus the room and use arrow keys and + / −.

About the materials

Stone surfaces use reference photographs from Venezia Stone; Midnight is an illustrative recolouring. These are not selected production slabs. Candidate references from Venezia Stone include India Green, Patagonia, Taj Mahal, and Onice Honey. Actual patterns, stock, thickness, backing, and support details require confirmation.

Model dimensions follow the concept brief. The rooms and accessories are illustrative settings. Interior models and surface maps include CC0 assets from Poly Haven. This is a desktop/mobile WebGL showroom; it does not include headset VR.
